text: ITR-1 (SAHAJ) is applicable to resident individuals having total income up to ₹50 lakh from salary, one house property, other sources, and agricultural income up to ₹5,000.
ITR-1 cannot be used by individuals who are directors in a company, have invested in unlisted equity shares, or have income from business or profession.
This section captures details of salary income received from one or more employers during the financial year.
Enter the gross basic salary received from your employer before claiming any deductions or exemptions.
Total income cannot exceed ₹50 lakh for filing ITR-1. If your income exceeds this limit, you must select a different ITR form.
This section is used to report income or loss from one self-occupied or let-out house property, including interest on borrowed capital.
Enter the interest paid on home loan during the financial year. For a self-occupied property, the deduction is capped as per applicable limits.
This section captures income such as savings bank interest, fixed deposit interest, family pension, and other taxable receipts.
Enter the total interest earned from savings bank accounts during the year. This income may be eligible for deduction under section 80TTA.
This section allows you to claim deductions under Chapter VI-A such as 80C, 80D, 80TTA, and other eligible deductions.
Enter investments or payments eligible for deduction under section 80C, such as LIC, PPF, EPF, ELSS, or tuition fees, subject to the prescribed limit.
This section computes tax liability based on total income, applicable slab rates, surcharge, cess, and eligible rebates.
Resident individuals with total income within the specified threshold may be eligible for rebate under section 87A, reducing tax liability.
Provide details of all savings and current bank accounts held during the year, and select one account for receiving income tax refund.
Refund cannot be issued unless at least one valid bank account is provided and marked for refund.
Report tax deducted/collected at source as per your Form 16/16A/26AS. Ensure PAN/TAN and amounts match the certificates.
Enter salary TDS details exactly as shown in Form 16, including employer TAN and tax deducted.
Enter details of advance tax and self-assessment tax paid during the year along with BSR code, date of deposit, and challan serial number.
If you paid self-assessment tax, ensure challan details (BSR, date, serial number) are correct to avoid credit mismatch.
Fill personal details such as PAN, Aadhaar, address, nature of employment, and filing status. These must match official records.
PAN and Aadhaar details must be valid and correctly linked/entered; incorrect identifiers can block filing or delay processing.
Select whether the house property is self-occupied or let-out and enter related income/interest details accordingly.
Report family pension, if any, under Other Sources and apply eligible deduction as per applicable provisions.
Complete verification by confirming the return details and choose a verification method (e-verification or ITR-V) to successfully submit the return.
Return filing is incomplete until verification is done. Ensure e-verification/ITR-V is completed within the allowed time to avoid invalid return.
